question: What is an AI agent, and when should one build an autonomous agent rather than plain code, a workflow, or a RAG system?
contributions: Defines autonomous agents on a spectrum of agency with the test of real decision making
Gives a four-factor decision guide: code vs workflow vs chatbot/RAG vs agent
Lists principles and organisational advice for agentic systems, and compares four frameworks

practices: Treat agency as a spectrum; the key test of a true agent is real decision making rather than following static scripts (Defining AI Agents).
Start with the latest general-purpose model from a leading provider, then experiment with smaller models, fine-tuning or retrieval to cut cost (Model Selection).
Route simple queries to small cheap models and reserve large models for complex reasoning; design for a multimodel future (Model Selection).
Use plain code when inputs are fully predictable, latency is millisecond-level, or regulated domains need deterministic auditable logic (Workflows and Agents).
Use a deterministic workflow when all branches can be enumerated and you need auditable control, retries with backoff or human approval (Workflows and Agents).
Use a chatbot or RAG when the need is question answering over a corpus with limited external actions (Workflows and Agents).
Use an autonomous agent for unstructured, novel or highly variable inputs needing dynamic multistep planning, parallel subtasks or learning from feedback (Workflows and Agents).

Before choosing an agent, ask whether inputs are unstructured, whether multistep adaptive planning is needed, whether retrieval suffices, and whether latency and maintenance burden are tolerable (Workflows and Agents).
Design for scalability, modularity, continuous learning, resilience and future-proofing (Principles section).
Avoid hardcoding tools in the agent service and avoid coupling to one vendor's prompt format (Principles section).
Add retry and fallback logic so a single API failure does not crash the agent (Principles section).
Encourage exploration early, then standardise 'one standard per large group'; adopt open standards such as OpenAPI; share lessons widely; keep governance lightweight (Organizing for Success).
For prototypes use CrewAI or OpenAI Agents SDK; for production-grade control use LangGraph or AutoGen; frameworks are optional (Agentic Frameworks).
